bibl.title: The Sixteenth Catechetical Homily — ܡܐܡܪܐ ܕܫܬܐ
The second homily on the Eucharist
bibl.author: Theodore of Mopsuestia — ܬܐܕܘܪܘܤ ܡܦܫܩܢܐ

noteGrp.note: On the Anaphora, the breaking of the bread, the Communion and the thanksgiving prayers at the end of mass. Theodore comments only on selected words of the Eucharistic prayer, e.g., the Sanctus that all the faithful recite. The epiclesis is an image of Christ’s resurrection, which also happened by the power of the Holy Spirit. After the Anaphora, the priest breaks the bread and puts the bread in the chalice piece by piece, which signifies Christ’s resurrection appearances to many people. The Eucharist will grant the remission of sins committed involuntarily, due to the weakness of human nature, if the recipients lament, demonstrate sorrow and repent. If a person committed a greater sin and repented, for this, confession, like medicine for sins, exists in the Church. Theodore teaches on the rules of private confession. Everyone who has sinned and wants to repent should go to priests and reveal their sins to them. They will not tell about the repentant’s sins to anyone.
